baseline: Host Linux 6.8.0-124-generic, prebuilt semctl02 from LTP 20260529 (/nix/store/hik6kb512ia3p14lc2vwzb292d4k306a-ltp-20260529, testcases copied to /tmp/ltpbase-qekfrt before running so nothing was written inside the store): 1 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped / 0 warnings, line 'semctl02.c:26: TPASS: semctl(IPC_STAT) with nobody user : EACCES (13)'. The test has exactly one assertion. setup() starts as root (needs_root=1), does SAFE_SETUID(65534) to become nobody, then SAFE_SEMGET(semkey, PSEMS=10, IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL) with NO permission bits, so the set is stamped mode 0 with uid=cuid=65534 and gid=cguid=0 (setuid changes only the uid, so egid stays root's). Per assertion: (1) semctl(sem_id, 0, IPC_STAT, un_arg) issued by the process that OWNS the set, whose mode is 0 => -1/EACCES(13). Then cleanup() calls SAFE_SEMCTL(sem_id, 0, IPC_RMID) still as nobody and it must SUCCEED - the host's 0 warnings prove it did, because IPC_RMID is governed by ownership rather than by the mode bits. Measured on the host with a purpose-written probe (/tmp/qekfrt-probe/ipcperm.c, ipcperm) rather than inferred, since the rule this test depends on is not the obvious one: for a set owned by the caller, mode 000 => IPC_STAT EACCES and SETVAL EACCES; mode 400 => IPC_STAT OK, SETVAL EACCES; mode 200 => IPC_STAT EACCES, SETVAL OK; mode 600 => both OK; and decisively mode 077 => BOTH EACCES, i.e. once the owner triplet is selected the group/other bits do not rescue the owner, so triplet selection is exclusive and not a union. A second probe (capprobe.c) confirms the CAP_IPC_OWNER escape: root, a non-owner, reads the same nobody-owned mode-0 set with IPC_STAT=OK, SETVAL=OK, IPC_RMID=OK, and reports back sem_perm.uid=65534 gid=0 mode=00, corroborating the stamping above. IPC_RMID by the unprivileged creator succeeded for every mode tested including 000.
failing_assertion: semctl02.c:26, the test's only assertion: 'TFAIL: semctl(IPC_STAT) with nobody user succeeded'. Asterinas's sys_semctl returned 0 and wrote a fully populated semid_ds into the caller's buffer, where the correct value is -1 with errno EACCES(13). Asterinas scores 0 passed / 1 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped / 0 warnings against the host's 1/0/0/0/0. Everything around the assertion worked: SAFE_SETUID(65534) and SAFE_SEMGET in setup() both succeeded, and the IPC_RMID in cleanup() also succeeded (0 warnings, no TBROK), so the defect is isolated to the permission decision for IPC_STAT and nothing else on the test's path is at fault.
root_cause: IpcNamespace::validate_sem_set (kernel/src/ipc/ipc_ns.rs:177-184) is a stub. Its signature binds the set as `_sem_set` and it never reads it: if the requested PermissionMode is non-empty it emits warn!("Semaphore doesn't support permission check now") and then returns Ok(()) unconditionally. It is the only permission gate in the SysV IPC code, so no IPC permission check exists anywhere in the kernel. semctl02 reaches it by this exact path: sys_semctl's IPC_STAT arm (kernel/src/syscall/semctl.rs:52-57) calls ipc_ns.with_sem_set(semid, PermissionMode::READ, ..); with_sem_set (ipc_ns.rs:94-107) calls Self::validate_sem_set(sem_set, required_perm)? at line 104; PermissionMode::READ is 0o004 (kernel/src/ipc/semaphore/system_v/mod.rs:14) hence non-empty, so the stub warns and returns Ok(()); control falls into `op(sem_set)`, which runs sem_set.semid_ds() and write_val's it to the user buffer, and sys_semctl returns SyscallReturn::Return(0) at semctl.rs:102. Note what is NOT wrong here, because it narrows the fix sharply: unlike the semget path at ipc_ns.rs:145 (which hardcodes ALTER|READ), semctl02's call site already passes the correct PermissionMode::READ, and the stored credentials are already correct and sufficient to decide the case - sys_semget computes mode = semflg & 0x1FF = 0 for IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL (semget.rs:9, since IPC_CREAT=0o1000 and IPC_EXCL=0o2000 are masked off by 0o777) and SemaphoreSet::new builds IpcPermission::new_sem_perm(key, credentials.euid(), credentials.egid(), mode) (sem_set.rs:252), with new_sem_perm setting cuid=uid and cguid=gid (ipc/mod.rs:102-111). So every input the decision needs is present and correct; validate_sem_set simply never consults any of it. The body of that one function is the whole defect on this test's path. Ruled out as contributing causes, each checked: (a) capability dropping works, so a future CAP_IPC_OWNER escape will not spuriously fire - set_resuid_unchecked (kernel/src/process/credentials/credentials_.rs:273-343) clears both permitted and effective capsets at lines 312-318 when had_root && all_nonroot, which is exactly the root->65534 transition setuid(65534) performs via set_uid (credentials_.rs:129-137); (b) the semid hash at ipc_ns.rs:133 does not collide, since the set is created fresh under a single key and setup() reported no error; (c) IPC_RMID does not pass through the stub at all - semctl.rs:36-51 hand-rolls euid == uid || euid == cuid and calls remove_sem_set, which is why cleanup already succeeds today and must keep succeeding.
invariant: Every operation on an existing System V IPC object other than removal or ownership change must be authorized against that object's stored ownership and mode before the operation is performed. The access bits the operation requires, folded from the read/write/execute triplets into a single low-three-bit request, must be a subset of exactly ONE triplet of the object's mode, chosen by the caller's credentials: the owner triplet when the caller's effective uid equals the object's owner uid or creator uid; otherwise the group triplet when the object's owner gid or creator gid is among the caller's groups; otherwise the other triplet. The selection is exclusive - a caller matching as owner is judged solely by the owner triplet and is denied even when the group or other triplets would have granted the access, so owning an object confers no access of its own and an object whose mode is 0 denies its own owner. A caller holding CAP_IPC_OWNER in the object's user namespace is exempt from the whole test. Object removal and ownership change are governed by a different and stricter rule that ignores the mode entirely: the caller must be the object's owner or creator, or hold CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
owning_layer: The shared System V IPC permission layer: the IpcPermission type in kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs (lines 57-112), with the predicate invoked from IpcNamespace in kernel/src/ipc/ipc_ns.rs where the validate_sem_set stub sits today. This is the closest Asterinas equivalent to Linux's ipcperms(), and Asterinas's structure already anticipates it: IpcPermission is a shared type that stores key/uid/gid/cuid/cguid/mode and nothing semaphore-specific, and ipc_ns.rs's own module doc (lines 5-7) says message queues and shared memory 'remain to be added'. The check must NOT live in SemaphoreSet or be open-coded in the individual sys_sem* handlers: the rule is byte-identical for message queues and shared memory, so putting it on IpcPermission means the future msgget/msgctl and shmget/shmctl paths inherit it instead of each re-deriving it, which is exactly the recurrence this field exists to prevent. Naming this layer matters even though the narrowest edit that turns semctl02 green is smaller than it: semctl02's call site at ipc_ns.rs:104 already passes the correct PermissionMode::READ, so filling in the stub body alone fixes this test - but the same stub is the only gate for five other semctl commands and for semget, so a fix aimed only at IPC_STAT would leave the identical hole reachable through every other command. PermissionMode (kernel/src/ipc/semaphore/system_v/mod.rs:10-16: ALTER=0o002, WRITE=0o002, READ=0o004) is already expressed in Linux's folded low-three-bit form and is the right argument type, though it currently lives under semaphore/system_v and would want to move up beside IpcPermission for msg/shm to reuse.
linux_reference: ipcperms() in ipc/util.c:553-572 (v6.8, fetched and read from git.kernel.org cgit; elixir.bootlin.com is blocked from this container). Its placement is the point: it lives in the shared IPC utility file, not in sem.c, msg.c or shm.c. Exact body: kuid_t euid = current_euid(); requested_mode = (flag >> 6) | (flag >> 3) | flag; granted_mode = ipcp->mode; if (uid_eq(euid, ipcp->cuid) || uid_eq(euid, ipcp->uid)) granted_mode >>= 6; else if (in_group_p(ipcp->cgid) || in_group_p(ipcp->gid)) granted_mode >>= 3; then if ((requested_mode & ~granted_mode & 0007) && !ns_capable(ns->user_ns, CAP_IPC_OWNER)) return -1. The `else if` is what makes triplet selection exclusive and is what my mode-077 host probe independently measured. semctl02's specific path is semctl_stat() in ipc/sem.c:1234, which at lines 1262-1264 does `err = -EACCES; if (ipcperms(ns, &sma->sem_perm, S_IRUGO)) goto out_unlock;` - so IPC_STAT requires S_IRUGO(0444), which folds to a requested_mode whose low three bits are 0o4, exactly Asterinas's PermissionMode::READ. The -EACCES mapping is set before the call, and on the semget path the same mapping is done by ipc_check_perms() (util.c:365-381). The other three ipcperms call sites in ipc/sem.c are 1263 (semctl_stat, S_IRUGO), 1368 (S_IWUGO), 1425 (cmd == SETALL ? S_IWUGO : S_IRUGO) and 2061 (semop, alter ? S_IWUGO : S_IRUGO). Crucially for this test's cleanup, IPC_RMID does NOT go through ipcperms: semctl_down uses ipcctl_obtain_check() (util.c:722-747), which checks uid_eq(euid, ipcp->cuid) || uid_eq(euid, ipcp->uid) || ns_capable(ns->user_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN) and returns -EPERM otherwise, never consulting the mode - which is why a nobody-owned mode-0 set can still be removed by its unprivileged creator, as both Linux and my host probe confirm. Asterinas already matches Linux on stamping: newary sets sem_perm.mode = semflg & S_IRWXUGO and ipc_addid sets cuid = uid = euid, gid = cgid = egid.
other_callers: Not narrow at all - this single stub is the only permission gate for every SysV IPC operation Asterinas implements, so they are all fixed or all missed together. Six sys_semctl commands already pass a meaningful PermissionMode into the stub and are therefore all unchecked today, meaning any process can currently read or overwrite any semaphore set in the namespace: PermissionMode::READ for IPC_STAT (semctl.rs:53), SEM_GETPID (62), SEM_GETVAL (72), SEM_GETNCNT (79) and SEM_GETZCNT (86), and PermissionMode::ALTER for SEM_SETVAL (96). All six route through ipc_ns.rs:104 with the correct mode already, so filling in the stub body fixes all six with no call-site change. sys_semget reaches the same stub from ipc_ns.rs:145 but needs a call-site change too, because that line hardcodes PermissionMode::ALTER | PermissionMode::READ instead of folding the caller's semflg the way Linux does; that is the defect the sibling run run-n8fKcM diagnosed for semget02 at this same commit e8f2b9ca6. sys_semop is the one caller that a correct predicate alone would still not fix: kernel/src/ipc/semaphore/system_v/sem.rs:212 and 289 pass PermissionMode::empty(), with a matching TODO at 199-200, so nothing would be authorized even after the stub is real; Linux checks alter ? S_IWUGO : S_IRUGO there and sem.rs:197 has already computed is_alter, so the call site needs ALTER or READ. sys_semctl(IPC_RMID) (semctl.rs:36-51) is deliberately outside this set: it bypasses validate_sem_set and hand-rolls euid == uid || euid == cuid, which matches Linux's separate ipcctl_obtain_check rule apart from the missing CAP_SYS_ADMIN admission, and it must stay outside - routing IPC_RMID through the mode-based predicate would break semctl02's own cleanup, since the set's mode is 0. Message queues and shared memory have no implementation yet, so nothing there is broken today, but they are precisely why the predicate belongs on IpcPermission rather than in semaphore code.
suggested_direction: Add the predicate to IpcPermission in kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs, e.g. `fn check_access(&self, requested: PermissionMode, credentials: &Credentials<ReadOp>) -> bool`, mirroring ipcperms(): take granted = self.mode(), shift it right 6 when credentials.euid() == self.uid() || credentials.euid() == self.cuid(), else right 3 when self.gid() or self.cguid() matches the caller's groups, else leave it unshifted; then the access is denied when requested.bits() & !granted & 0o7 != 0. Keep the branches as an exclusive if / else if / else chain - not a union of triplets - since the mode-077 probe shows an owner must be denied despite permissive group/other bits. All inputs already exist: static_cap.rs exposes euid() (line 62), egid() (163), fsgid() (179) and groups() (256, a BTreeSet<Gid>), and IpcPermission already stores every field needed. Then de-stub validate_sem_set (ipc_ns.rs:177-184) to call it and map denial to EACCES. The CAP_IPC_OWNER escape should use the namespace-scoped hook already used at ipc_ns.rs:85-89: lsm_hooks::on_capable(lsm_hooks::CapableContext::new(self.owner.as_ref(), posix_thread, CapSet::IPC_OWNER)); CapSet::IPC_OWNER is defined at kernel/src/process/credentials/capabilities.rs:26 and is currently unused. That escape carries the one trap most likely to silently defeat this fix: on_capable returns Err(EPERM) when the capability is absent (kernel/src/security/lsm/modules/capability.rs:28-46), so its error must be swallowed and converted into the EACCES denial rather than propagated - propagating it would make semctl02 fail with EPERM(1) instead of EACCES(13) and the assertion would still not pass. The structural cost is threading: validate_sem_set is a static fn today with no &self, and it needs &self (for self.owner) plus the caller's PosixThread or Credentials, so with_sem_set must take them and its seven call sites (five in semctl.rs, two in sem.rs) must pass them; ctx.posix_thread and ctx.posix_thread.credentials() are already in scope at every semctl.rs site. Leave create_sem_set and the insert_at arm of get_or_create_sem_set unchecked, matching Linux's ipcget_new, which performs no permission check on creation.

Scope limit worth stating plainly so the fix is not over-trusted: because this set's mode is 0, EVERY triplet of it is 0, so semctl02 by itself only pins that a check exists at all and that owning an object grants nothing - it does NOT discriminate triplet selection, and a fix that wrongly ORed the triplets or fell through to the group branch would still pass it. The mode-077 and mode-400/200/600 host probes above are what pin the selection rule, and phase 4 should lean on them plus the regression tests rather than on this one assertion. Regression risk is low but real: semctl07 (all.txt:1338), semget01 (1342) and semop03 (1348) are already enabled and currently pass with permission checks disabled; all three create their sets with SEM_RA (0600) and run as root, whose owner triplet is 6 = READ|ALTER and who additionally holds CAP_IPC_OWNER, so a faithful check should leave them green. semctl02's own cleanup is the sharper trap - it does IPC_RMID as the unprivileged owner of a mode-0 set, so the existing euid check in the IPC_RMID arm (semctl.rs:36-51) must keep letting it through and must not be rerouted through the new mode-based predicate.
